hindi: व्यसनों के एक साथ आ पड़ने पर, सुगमता के अनुसार चढ़ाई करनी चाहिए या रक्षा करनी चाहिए — इस प्रकार का विचार व्यसनचिन्ता है।
english: When calamities (vyasana) occur simultaneously, whether one is to march or to protect, according to ease — this is the consideration of calamities.
notes: Chapter heading-sentence. vyasana rendered 'calamity' (व्यसन) throughout this chunk. yātavyam/rakṣitavyam are impersonal gerundives: 'is one to march or to protect'.
lines_deva: व्यसन.यौगपद्ये सौकर्यतो यातव्यं रक्षितव्यं वा-इति व्यसन.चिन्ता
lines_iast: vyasana.yaugapadye saukaryato yātavyaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ vā-iti vyasana.cintā

hindi: प्रकृति का व्यसन, दैव हो या मानुष, अनय और अपनय से उत्पन्न होता है।
english: A calamity of a constituent element, divine or human, arises from misfortune and from bad policy.
notes: anaya/apanaya as in glossary (6.2): misfortune / bad policy; the divine calamity from anaya, the human from apanaya is the natural pairing but the text only lists both.
lines_deva: दैवं मानुषं वा प्रकृति.व्यसनम् अनय.अपनयाभ्यां सम्भवति
lines_iast: daivaṃ mānuṣaṃ vā prakṛti.vyasanam anaya.apanayābhyāṃ sambhavati

hindi: गुणों की प्रतिकूलता, अभाव, बड़ा दोष, आसक्ति अथवा पीड़ा — यह व्यसन है।
english: A calamity is the reversal of excellences, absence, a grave defect, excessive attachment, or affliction.
notes: pradoṣa could also be 'vice'; prasaṅga 'addiction' (to vices). Literal renderings kept.
lines_deva: गुण.प्रातिलोम्यम् अभावः प्रदोषः प्रसङ्गः पीडा वा व्यसनम्
lines_iast: guṇa.prātilomyam abhāvaḥ pradoṣaḥ prasaṅgaḥ pīḍā vā vyasanam

hindi: यह उसे श्रेय से दूर फेंक देता है, इसलिए यह व्यसन कहलाता है।
english: It casts him away from well-being — hence it is called a calamity (vyasana).
notes: Etymological definition: vyasana from vi-√as 'cast away'.

words.gloss: of the calamities of king, minister, country, fort, treasury, army and ally

hindi: “स्वामी, अमात्य, जनपद, दुर्ग, कोश, दण्ड और मित्र के व्यसनों में पहले-पहले का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है” — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: 'Among the calamities of the king, the minister, the country, the fort, the treasury, the army and the ally, each preceding one is more serious,' say the teachers.
notes: pūrvam pūrvam (repetition) = 'each earlier one in the list'. The opening quotation mark belongs to the edition's punctuation.

hindi: “नहीं” — ऐसा भरद्वाज कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Bharadvaja.

words.gloss: of the calamities of king and minister

hindi: “स्वामी और अमात्य के व्यसनों में अमात्य का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है।
english: 'Between the calamities of the king and the minister, the calamity of the minister is more serious.
notes: Bharadvaja's argument begins here and runs to unit 11 (closing quote there).

words.gloss: attainment of the fruit of counsel
the business of income and expenditure
warding off of enemies and forest-tribes

hindi: मन्त्रणा, मन्त्रणा के फल की प्राप्ति, कार्यों का सम्पादन, आय-व्यय का कार्य, दण्ड का प्रणयन, शत्रुओं और आटविकों का निवारण, राज्य की रक्षा, व्यसनों का प्रतीकार, कुमारों की रक्षा और कुमारों का अभिषेक — ये सब अमात्यों पर निर्भर हैं।
english: Counsel, the attainment of the fruit of counsel, the carrying out of works, the business of income and expenditure, the administration of punishment, the warding off of enemies and forest-tribes, the protection of the kingdom, the remedying of calamities, the protection of the princes and the consecration of the princes depend on the ministers.
notes: daṇḍa-praṇayana: 'administration of punishment (daṇḍa)'; could also be taken as 'use of force / deployment of the army'. āyattam is n. sg. agreeing loosely with the whole list (sense: 'all this is dependent'). aṭavī = forest-tribe (forest-dwellers), literally 'forest'.
lines_deva: मन्त्रो मन्त्र.फल.अवाप्तिः कर्म.अनुष्ठानम् आय.व्यय.कर्म दण्ड.प्रणयनम् अमित्र.अटवी.प्रतिषेधो राज्य.रक्षणं व्यसन.प्रतीकारः कुमार.रक्षणम् अभिषेकश् च कुमाराणाम् आयत्तम् अमात्येषु
lines_iast: mantro mantra.phala.avāptiḥ karma.anuṣṭhānam āya.vyaya.karma daṇḍa.praṇayanam amitra.aṭavī.pratiṣedho rājya.rakṣaṇaṃ vyasana.pratīkāraḥ kumāra.rakṣaṇam abhiṣekaś ca kumārāṇām āyattam amātyeṣu

words.gloss: of one whose wings are cut

hindi: उनके अभाव में इन सबका अभाव हो जाता है, और जिसके पंख कट गए हों उसकी भाँति राजा की चेष्टा का भी नाश हो जाता है।
english: In their absence those (functions) are absent, and, as with one whose wings are cut, there is loss of activity for the king.
notes: tad- refers back to the list of functions in unit 8. chinna-pakṣa 'wing-clipped' (a bird is implied, not stated).
lines_deva: तेषाम् अभावे तद्.अभावः, छिन्न.पक्षस्य-इव राज्ञश् चेष्टा.नाशश् च
lines_iast: teṣām abhāve tad.abhāvaḥ, chinna.pakṣasya-iva rājñaś ceṣṭā.nāśaś ca

hindi: और उनके व्यसनों में शत्रु का उपजाप निकट आ जाता है।
english: And in their calamities, secret instigation by the enemy is near at hand.
notes: upajāpa = secret instigation/sowing of dissension by the enemy among the king's men. 'their' (the ministers') is implied by context.

words.gloss: because of moving close to (his) life

hindi: और उनके विगुण हो जाने पर राजा के प्राणों को बाधा होती है, क्योंकि वे राजा के प्राणों के समीप विचरण करते हैं।”
english: And when they become defective, there is danger to the king's life, because they move close to his life (person).'
notes: vaiguṇya = defect/turning bad of the ministers. prāṇa-antika-cara = one who moves near the (king's) life, i.e. in close bodily proximity to him. Closing quote ends Bharadvaja's view (units 7-11). vaiguṇya: 'defectiveness' kept literal; it is often understood as the ministers turning hostile or disloyal. rājñaḥ occurs once and goes with prāṇa-antika-caratvāt; 'the king's' before 'life' in the first clause is understood.
lines_deva: वैगुण्ये च प्राण.आबाधः प्राण.अन्तिक.चरत्वाद् राज्ञः" इति
lines_iast: vaiguṇye ca prāṇa.ābādhaḥ prāṇa.antika.caratvād rājñaḥ" iti

hindi: “नहीं” — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.

words.gloss: the body of servants beginning with councillor and chaplain
remedying of calamities of the human and material constituents

hindi: मन्त्री, पुरोहित आदि भृत्यवर्ग को, अध्यक्षों के कार्य-संचालन को, पुरुष-प्रकृतियों और द्रव्य-प्रकृतियों के व्यसनों के प्रतीकार को और उनकी वृद्धि को राजा ही करता है।
english: It is the king alone who makes the body of servants headed by the councillor and the chaplain, the activity of the superintendents, the remedying of the calamities of the human and material constituent elements, and their prospering.
notes: karoti governs all four accusatives: 'appoints' the servants, 'directs' the superintendents' activity, 'effects' the remedying, 'brings about' the prospering. puruṣa-prakṛti / dravya-prakṛti = human (king, minister...) and material (fort, treasury...) constituents, as in 6.2.
lines_deva: मन्त्रि.पुरोहित.आदि.भृत्य.वर्गम् अध्यक्ष.प्रचारं पुरुष.द्रव्य.प्रकृति.व्यसन.प्रतीकारम् एधनं च राजा-एव करोति
lines_iast: mantri.purohita.ādi.bhṛtya.vargam adhyakṣa.pracāraṃ puruṣa.dravya.prakṛti.vyasana.pratīkāram edhanaṃ ca rājā-eva karoti

hindi: अथवा अमात्यों के व्यसनग्रस्त होने पर वह दूसरे व्यसनरहित व्यक्तियों को अमात्य बनाता है।
english: Or, when the ministers are afflicted by calamity, he makes others, free from calamity, (ministers).
notes: vyasaniṣu amātyeṣu: locative absolute.

words.gloss: in honouring those who deserve honour

hindi: वह पूज्यों के सम्मान और दूष्यों के निग्रह में सदा लगा रहता है।
english: He remains ever intent on honouring those who deserve honour and on restraining the treasonable.
notes: dūṣya = the treasonable (glossary 6.2).

hindi: और सम्पन्न स्वामी अपनी सम्पत्तियों से प्रकृतियों को सम्पन्न बनाता है।
english: And the king, endowed with excellences, makes the constituent elements excellent by his own excellences.
notes: sampat = excellence (glossary).
lines_deva: स्वामी च सम्पन्नः स्व.सम्पद्भिः प्रकृतीः सम्पादयति
lines_iast: svāmī ca sampannaḥ sva.sampadbhiḥ prakṛtīḥ sampādayati

hindi: वह जैसे स्वभाव का होता है, प्रकृतियाँ वैसे ही स्वभाव की हो जाती हैं, क्योंकि उद्यम और प्रमाद में वे उसी पर निर्भर हैं।
english: Of whatever character he is, of that character the constituent elements become, because in exertion and in negligence they are dependent on him.
lines_deva: स यत्.शीलस् तत्.शीलाः प्रकृतयो भवन्ति, उत्थाने प्रमादे च तद्.आयत्तत्वात्
lines_iast: sa yat.śīlas tat.śīlāḥ prakṛtayo bhavanti, utthāne pramāde ca tad.āyattatvāt

words.gloss: standing in the position of their summit

hindi: क्योंकि स्वामी उनके शिखर के स्थान पर होता है।
english: For the king stands in the position of their summit (head).
notes: kūṭa = summit/peak, i.e. the head on which the others depend; iti closes Kautilya's reply (units 13-18).

words.gloss: of the calamities of minister and country

hindi: “अमात्य और जनपद के व्यसनों में जनपद का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है” — ऐसा विशालाक्ष कहते हैं।
english: 'Between the calamities of the minister and the country, the calamity of the country is more serious,' says Vishalaksha.

hindi: “कोश, दण्ड, कुप्य द्रव्य, विष्टि-श्रम, वाहन और संचय जनपद से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: 'The treasury, the army, raw materials (kupya), forced labour, conveyances and stores arise from the country.
notes: Vishalaksha's argument, units 20-21. kupya = raw materials from forests (timber, metals etc.); vāhana = means of transport / draught animals.
lines_deva: "कोशो दण्डः कुप्यं विष्टिर् वाहनं निचयाश् च जन.पदाद् उत्तिष्ठन्ते
lines_iast: "kośo daṇḍaḥ kupyaṃ viṣṭir vāhanaṃ nicayāś ca jana.padād uttiṣṭhante

words.gloss: in the absence of the country

hindi: जनपद के अभाव में इनका अभाव होता है, और उसके तुरन्त बाद स्वामी और अमात्य का भी अभाव हो जाता है।”
english: In the absence of the country these are absent, and (the absence) of the king and the minister follows immediately.'
notes: anantaraḥ agrees with abhāvaḥ: 'the (absence) of king and minister is next'.
lines_deva: तेषाम् अभावो जन.पद.अभावे, स्वाम्य्.अमात्ययोश् च-अनन्तरः" इति
lines_iast: teṣām abhāvo jana.pada.abhāve, svāmy.amātyayoś ca-anantaraḥ" iti

hindi: “नहीं” — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.

hindi: सब आरम्भों के मूल अमात्य हैं — जनपद के कार्यों की सिद्धि, अपनी ओर से और दूसरे की ओर से योग-क्षेम का साधन, व्यसनों का प्रतीकार, शून्य भूमि का निवेश और उसकी वृद्धि, तथा दण्ड और कर में अनुग्रह।
english: All undertakings have the ministers as their root: the successes of the country's works, the securing of acquisition and security from one's own side and from the other's, the remedying of calamities, the settling of empty land and its growth, and favour in the matter of fines and taxes.
notes: daṇḍa here = fines (daṇḍa-kara 'fines and taxes'), not the army. svataḥ parataḥ: from the king's own side and from the enemy's side. The dash is the edition's punctuation, introducing the list.
lines_deva: अमात्य.मूलाः सर्व.आरम्भाः - जन.पदस्य कर्म.सिद्धयः स्वतः परतश् च योग.क्षेम.साधनं व्यसन.प्रतीकारः शून्य.निवेश.उपचयौ दण्ड.कर.अनुग्रहश् च-इति
lines_iast: amātya.mūlāḥ sarva.ārambhāḥ - jana.padasya karma.siddhayaḥ svataḥ parataś ca yoga.kṣema.sādhanaṃ vyasana.pratīkāraḥ śūnya.niveśa.upacayau daṇḍa.kara.anugrahaś ca-iti

words.gloss: of the calamities of country and fort

hindi: “जनपद और दुर्ग के व्यसनों में दुर्ग का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है” — ऐसा पाराशर कहते हैं।
english: 'Between the calamities of the country and the fort, the calamity of the fort (is more serious),' say the Parasharas.
notes: garīyaḥ 'is more serious' is understood from units 5, 7, 19 and supplied in translation. pārāśarāḥ = the followers of Parashara (a school).

hindi: “क्योंकि दुर्ग में कोश और दण्ड की उत्पत्ति होती है, और आपत्ति में जनपद का आश्रय-स्थान भी वही है।
english: 'For in the fort lies the origin of the treasury and the army, and (it is) a refuge for the country in adversity.
notes: Parasharas' argument, units 25-27. Token 'kośa.-daṇḍa.utpattir' carries both a compound mark and the join mark in the e-text; read as one compound kośa-daṇḍa-utpattiḥ. sthāna = place (of refuge).
lines_deva: "दुर्गे हि कोश.-दण्ड.उत्पत्तिर् आपदि स्थानं च जन.पदस्य
lines_iast: "durge hi kośa.-daṇḍa.utpattir āpadi sthānaṃ ca jana.padasya

hindi: और नगरवासी जनपदवासियों से अधिक शक्तिशाली होते हैं और आपत्ति में राजा के नित्य सहायक होते हैं।
english: And the townsmen are more powerful than the country people, and are constant helpers of the king in adversity.
notes: paura = inhabitants of the (fortified) town; jānapada = inhabitants of the countryside.
lines_deva: शक्तिमत्तराश् च पौरा जानपदेभ्यो नित्याश् च-आपदि सहाया राज्ञः
lines_iast: śaktimattarāś ca paurā jānapadebhyo nityāś ca-āpadi sahāyā rājñaḥ

hindi: किन्तु जनपदवासी तो शत्रु के भी साझे होते हैं।”
english: But the country people are shared with the enemy (too).'
notes: amitra-sādhāraṇa = common to (accessible to, usable by) the enemy as well. Closing quote ends the Parasharas' view.

hindi: “नहीं” — ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: 'No,' says Kautilya.

words.gloss: undertakings of fort, treasury, army, embankments and economic activity

hindi: दुर्ग, कोश, दण्ड, सेतु और वार्ता के आरम्भों का मूल जनपद है।
english: The undertakings of the fort, the treasury, the army, embankments (irrigation works) and vārttā (economic activity) have the country as their root.
notes: setu = embankment/dam, i.e. irrigation works; vārttā = the science of livelihood (agriculture, cattle-rearing, trade). Kautilya's reply, units 29-32.

hindi: शौर्य, स्थिरता, दक्षता और बाहुल्य जनपदवासियों में होते हैं।
english: Bravery, steadfastness, skill and abundance (of numbers) are found in the country people.
notes: bāhulya = being numerous; 'are found' supplies the verb.
lines_deva: शौर्यं स्थैर्यं दाक्ष्यं बाहुल्यं च जानपदेषु
lines_iast: śauryaṃ sthairyaṃ dākṣyaṃ bāhulyaṃ ca jānapadeṣu

words.gram: m. nom. pl. (dvandva, as adj. to durgāḥ)

words.gloss: because of the absence of the country

hindi: और पर्वतों तथा नदी-द्वीपों के दुर्ग जनपद के अभाव में बसाए नहीं जाते।
english: And forts on mountains and river-islands are not inhabited in the absence of the country.
notes: parvata-antardvīpāḥ durgāḥ: 'mountain- and island-forts' (bahuvrīhi-like use of the dvandva as adjective to durgāḥ, here masculine). antar-dvīpa = island within a river.

words.gloss: in (a country) consisting mostly of cultivators

hindi: किन्तु किसानों की प्रधानता वाले जनपद में दुर्ग का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है, और योद्धाओं की प्रधानता वाले जनपद में जनपद का व्यसन।
english: But in a country consisting mostly of cultivators, the calamity of the fort (is more serious); in a country consisting mostly of soldiers, the calamity of the country (is more serious).
notes: garīyaḥ is understood (ellipsis) in both halves; jana-pade of the second half is to be taken with the first half too. iti closes Kautilya's reply.
lines_deva: कर्षक.प्राये तु दुर्ग.व्यसनम्, आयुधीय.प्राये तु जन.पदे जन.पद.व्यसनम् इति
lines_iast: karṣaka.prāye tu durga.vyasanam, āyudhīya.prāye tu jana.pade jana.pada.vyasanam iti

words.gloss: of the calamities of the fort and the treasury
words.gram: n. loc. du. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

hindi: “दुर्ग और कोश के व्यसनों में कोश का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है,” ऐसा पिशुन कहते हैं।
english: “Of the calamities of the fort and the treasury, that of the treasury (is more serious),” says Pishuna.
notes: The predicate 'is the graver' (garīyaḥ) is not in this line; it is understood from the chapter's pattern (cf. 8.1.52 garīyaḥ).

words.gloss: having the treasury as its root
the building up of the fort
keeping in check the country, the ally and the enemy
words.gram: m. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

words.gloss: the employment of the forces of the army

hindi: “क्योंकि दुर्ग का निर्माण, दुर्ग की रक्षा, जनपद, मित्र और अमित्र का निग्रह, दूर देशों में स्थित लोगों को उत्साहित करना और दण्ड के बल का व्यवहार — इन सबका मूल कोश है।
english: “For the building up of the fort, the guarding of the fort, keeping in check the country, the ally and the enemy, the inciting of those in distant lands, and the employment of the forces of the army have the treasury as their root.
notes: Pishuna's view continues to 8.1.36. kośa-mūlaḥ (masc.) agrees with the first item durga-saṃskāraḥ; the predicate applies to the whole list. deśa-antaritānām could also mean 'those cut off by distance'. daṇḍa-bala-vyavahāra could also be read 'the use of army and force'.
lines_deva: "कोश.मूलो हि दुर्ग.संस्कारो दुर्ग.रक्षणं जन.पद.मित्र.अमित्र.निग्रहो देश.अन्तरितानाम् उत्साहनं दण्ड.बल.व्यवहारश् च
lines_iast: "kośa.mūlo hi durga.saṃskāro durga.rakṣaṇaṃ jana.pada.mitra.amitra.nigraho deśa.antaritānām utsāhanaṃ daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāraś ca

words.gloss: liable to be won over by secret instigation

hindi: शत्रुओं के कोश से दुर्ग को उपजाप द्वारा फोड़ा जा सकता है।
english: The fort can be won over by secret instigation by means of the enemies' treasury.
notes: pareṣām is taken with kośāt ('the enemies' treasury'); it could instead be the agent of the gerundive ('can be instigated by the enemies, by means of treasure').

hindi: और व्यसन में कोश को लेकर भाग जाना सम्भव है, दुर्ग को लेकर नहीं।”
english: And in a calamity it is possible to go away taking the treasury, but not the fort.”
notes: iti closes Pishuna's view (8.1.33-36).
lines_deva: कोशम् आदाय च व्यसने शक्यम् अपयातुम्, न दुर्गम्" इति
lines_iast: kośam ādāya ca vyasane śakyam apayātum, na durgam" iti

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

words.gloss: keeping one's own party in check
the employment of the forces of the army
the warding off of the enemy's army and forest tribes

hindi: कोश, दण्ड, तूष्णीं-युद्ध, अपने पक्ष का निग्रह, दण्ड के बल का व्यवहार, आसार का प्रतिग्रह, तथा शत्रु-सेना और आटवी का प्रतिषेध — ये सब दुर्ग पर आश्रित हैं।
english: The treasury, the army, silent war, keeping one's own party in check, the employment of the forces of the army, the receiving of a reinforcer, and the warding off of the enemy's army and forest tribes rest on the fort.
notes: durga-arpaṇaḥ 'having its placing in the fort' = dependent on the fort; it agrees with kośaḥ but governs the whole list. tūṣṇīṃ-yuddha = 'silent war' (secret measures), kept literal. aṭavī = forest (tribes).
lines_deva: दुर्ग.अर्पणः कोशो दण्डस् तूष्णीं.युद्धं स्व.पक्ष.निग्रहो दण्ड.बल.व्यवहार आसार.प्रतिग्रहः पर.चक्र.अटवी.प्रतिषेधश् च
lines_iast: durga.arpaṇaḥ kośo daṇḍas tūṣṇīṃ.yuddhaṃ sva.pakṣa.nigraho daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāra āsāra.pratigrahaḥ para.cakra.aṭavī.pratiṣedhaś ca

words.gloss: in the absence of a fort

hindi: और दुर्ग के अभाव में कोश शत्रुओं का हो जाता है।
english: And in the absence of a fort, the treasury becomes the enemies'.

hindi: क्योंकि दुर्गवालों का उच्छेद न होना देखा जाता है।
english: For it is seen that those who possess forts are not exterminated.
notes: iti closes Kautilya's reply (8.1.37-40). The closing iti is not rendered by a separate phrase (the reply is unquoted in the e-text).

words.gloss: of the calamities of the treasury and the army
words.gram: n. loc. du. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

hindi: “कोश और दण्ड के व्यसनों में दण्ड का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है,” ऐसा कौणपदन्त कहते हैं।
english: “Of the calamities of the treasury and the army, that of the army (is more serious),” says Kaunapadanta.
notes: The e-text writes 'daṇḍavyasanayor' without the compound dot between daṇḍa and vyasana; the text itself is sound. Predicate 'is the graver' understood as in 8.1.33.

words.gloss: having the army as its root
keeping the ally and the enemy in check
words.gram: m. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

words.gloss: the inciting of the enemy's army
the holding together of one's own army

hindi: “क्योंकि मित्र और अमित्र का निग्रह, शत्रु के दण्ड को उत्साहित करना और अपने दण्ड को सँभाले रखना — इन सबका मूल दण्ड है।
english: “For keeping the ally and the enemy in check, the inciting of the enemy's army, and the holding together of one's own army have the army as their root.
notes: Kaunapadanta's view continues to 8.1.45. pratigraha = 'receiving, keeping hold of'; sva-daṇḍa-pratigraha could also mean 'the winning over of one's own troops'. pratigraha is also the technical term for the army's reserve force (Book 10), so 'keeping a reserve of one's own army' is another possible reading.

words.gloss: in the absence of an army

hindi: और दण्ड के अभाव में कोश का विनाश निश्चित है।
english: And in the absence of an army, the destruction of the treasury is certain.

words.gloss: in the absence of a treasury
by seizing the enemy's land for oneself
by one who possesses an army

hindi: और कोश के अभाव में दण्ड को कुप्य से, भूमि से, अथवा शत्रु की भूमि को स्वयं हड़प लेने से एकत्र रखा जा सकता है; और दण्डवान् के द्वारा कोश एकत्र किया जा सकता है।
english: And in the absence of a treasury the army can be held together by means of raw materials, land, or the seizing of the enemy's land for oneself; and by one who possesses an army a treasury can be gathered.
notes: kupya = raw materials (forest produce), per glossary. 'can be gathered' in the last clause is carried over from śakyaḥ ... piṇḍayitum.
lines_deva: कोश.अभावे च शक्यः कुप्येन भूम्या पर.भूमि.स्वयं.ग्राहेण वा दण्डः पिण्डयितुम्, दण्डवता च कोशः
lines_iast: kośa.abhāve ca śakyaḥ kupyena bhūmyā para.bhūmi.svayaṃ.grāheṇa vā daṇḍaḥ piṇḍayitum, daṇḍavatā ca kośaḥ

words.gloss: sharing the nature of the minister

hindi: और स्वामी के निकट रहने के कारण दण्ड अमात्य के समान धर्म वाला है।”
english: And because of its close attendance on the king, the army shares the nature of the minister.”
notes: iti closes Kaunapadanta's view (8.1.41-45). svāminaḥ (gen.) is construed with āsanna-vṛttitvāt.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

words.gloss: having the treasury as its root

hindi: क्योंकि दण्ड का मूल कोश है।
english: For the army has the treasury as its root.

words.gloss: in the absence of a treasury

hindi: कोश के अभाव में दण्ड शत्रु के पास चला जाता है, अथवा स्वामी को मार डालता है।
english: In the absence of a treasury the army goes over to the enemy, or kills the king.
lines_deva: कोश.अभावे दण्डः परं गच्छति, स्वामिनं वा हन्ति
lines_iast: kośa.abhāve daṇḍaḥ paraṃ gacchati, svāminaṃ vā hanti

words.gloss: the means of dharma and pleasure
words.gram: m. nom. sg. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

hindi: और कोश सब अभियोगों का साधक तथा धर्म और काम का हेतु है।
english: And the treasury brings about every undertaking and is the means of dharma and pleasure.
notes: abhiyoga = undertaking, attack (military enterprise).

words.gloss: according to place, time and task
words.gram: m. inst. sg. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

words.gloss: of the treasury and the army

hindi: किन्तु देश, काल और कार्य के अनुसार कोश और दण्ड में से कोई एक प्रधान हो जाता है।
english: But according to place, time and task, one or the other of the treasury and the army becomes the deciding factor.
notes: pramāṇī-bhavati 'becomes the standard', i.e. the more important of the two.

hindi: क्योंकि दण्ड कोश के लाभ और पालन का साधन होता है, और कोश कोश और दण्ड दोनों के लाभ और पालन का साधन होता है।
english: For the army serves for the acquisition and protection of the treasury, while the treasury serves for that of both the treasury and the army.
notes: lambha-pālanaḥ is understood again in the second clause.
lines_deva: लम्भ.पालनो हि दण्डः कोशस्य, कोशः कोशस्य दण्डस्य च भवति
lines_iast: lambha.pālano hi daṇḍaḥ kośasya, kośaḥ kośasya daṇḍasya ca bhavati

words.gloss: because it sets all things in motion

hindi: सब द्रव्यों का प्रयोजक होने के कारण कोश का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है।
english: Because it sets all things in motion, the calamity of the treasury is the more serious.
notes: iti closes Kautilya's reply (8.1.46-52). dravya = things, materials (resources).

words.gloss: of the calamities of the army and the ally
words.gram: n. loc. du. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first member)

hindi: “दण्ड और मित्र के व्यसनों में मित्र का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है,” ऐसा वातव्याधि कहते हैं।
english: “Of the calamities of the army and the ally, that of the ally (is more serious),” says Vatavyadhi.
notes: Predicate 'is the graver' understood as in 8.1.33.

words.gloss: at the juncture of a state of calamity

hindi: “मित्र बिना वेतन के और दूर रहते हुए भी कार्य करता है; पार्ष्णिग्राह, आसार, शत्रु और आटविक का प्रतिकार करता है; और व्यसन की अवस्था आने पर कोश, दण्ड और भूमि से सहायता करता है।”
english: “The ally, unpaid and at a distance, does work; it counteracts the heel-seizer, the reinforcer, the enemy and the forest chief; and when a state of calamity arises it helps with treasury, army and land.”
notes: Vatavyadhi's view, closed by iti. abhṛtam and vyavahitam are taken with mitram (the ally, though unpaid and distant, does work); they could instead qualify karma ('does work that is unpaid and distant'). vyasana-avasthā-yogam read as an adverbial accusative of occasion.
lines_deva: "मित्रम् अभृतं व्यवहितं च कर्म करोति, पार्ष्णि.ग्राहम् आसारम् अमित्रम् आटविकं च प्रतिकरोति, कोश.दण्ड.भूमिभिश् च-उपकरोति व्यसन.अवस्था.योगम्" इति
lines_iast: "mitram abhṛtaṃ vyavahitaṃ ca karma karoti, pārṣṇi.grāham āsāram amitram āṭavikaṃ ca pratikaroti, kośa.daṇḍa.bhūmibhiś ca-upakaroti vyasana.avasthā.yogam" iti

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

words.gloss: of one who possesses an army
in the condition of an ally
in the condition of an ally

hindi: दण्डवान् का मित्र मित्र-भाव में बना रहता है, अथवा शत्रु मित्र-भाव में आ जाता है।
english: For one who possesses an army the ally remains in the condition of an ally, or the enemy comes to be in the condition of an ally.
notes: 'comes to be' in the second clause carries over tiṣṭhati.
lines_deva: दण्डवतो मित्रं मित्र.भावे तिष्ठति, अमित्रो वा मित्र.भावे
lines_iast: daṇḍavato mitraṃ mitra.bhāve tiṣṭhati, amitro vā mitra.bhāve

words.gloss: of the army and the ally
from the advantage of place and time for one's own fighting

hindi: किन्तु दण्ड और मित्र में, दोनों के लिए समान कार्य में, सार की दृष्टि से तथा अपने युद्ध के लिए देश और काल के लाभ की दृष्टि से विशेषता होती है।
english: But between the army and the ally, in a task common to both, the distinction is in point of strength and from the advantage of place and time for one's own fighting.
notes: sāra = substance, strength (of the force). The compound could also be split sva-yuddha / deśa-kāla-lābha: 'own fighting, and the gain of place and time'.
lines_deva: दण्ड.मित्रयोस् तु साधारणे कार्ये सारतः स्व.युद्ध.देश.काल.लाभाद् विशेषः
lines_iast: daṇḍa.mitrayos tu sādhāraṇe kārye sārataḥ sva.yuddha.deśa.kāla.lābhād viśeṣaḥ

words.gloss: in an uprising of an enemy or forest chief from outside
words.gram: m. loc. sg. (tat-puruṣa, dvandva in first members)

hindi: किन्तु शीघ्र अभियान में तथा बाहर के शत्रु या आटविक के कोप में मित्र उपलब्ध नहीं होता।
english: But in a swift expedition, and in an uprising of an enemy or forest chief who is not in the interior, no ally is found.
notes: anabhyantara = 'not internal', i.e. an outsider; the sense is that the ally is of no avail in these cases. anabhyantara could also be a third dvandva member: 'in a revolt of the enemy, the forest chief or one not of the interior (an outsider)'.
lines_deva: शीघ्र.अभियाने त्व् अमित्र.आटविक.अनभ्यन्तर.कोपे च न मित्रं विद्यते
lines_iast: śīghra.abhiyāne tv amitra.āṭavika.anabhyantara.kope ca na mitraṃ vidyate

words.gloss: where there is a connection with gain

hindi: व्यसनों के एक साथ आने पर और शत्रु की वृद्धि होने पर मित्र अर्थ का सम्बन्ध होने पर टिकता है।
english: When calamities occur simultaneously and when the enemy grows, the ally stands firm where there is a connection with gain.
notes: artha-yukti 'connection with gain': the sense is that the ally stays while it is in its interest; this emphasis is not rendered in the translation.
lines_deva: व्यसन.यौगपद्ये पर.वृद्धौ च मित्रम् अर्थ.युक्तौ तिष्ठति
lines_iast: vyasana.yaugapadye para.vṛddhau ca mitram artha.yuktau tiṣṭhati

words.gloss: the deliberation on the calamities of the constituent elements

hindi: इस प्रकार प्रकृतियों के व्यसनों का सम्प्रधारण कहा गया।
english: Thus the deliberation on the calamities of the constituent elements has been stated.

words.gloss: of the parts of a constituent element

hindi: किन्तु प्रकृति के अवयवों के व्यसन में विशेष रूप से उनकी बहुसंख्या, अनुराग अथवा सार ही कार्य का साधक होता है।
english: But as regards the calamity of the parts of a constituent element in particular, it is numerousness, or loyalty, or strength that accomplishes the task.
notes: prakṛty-avayavānāṃ vyasanasya: genitive of reference ('in the calamity of the parts'). Two half-lines of 16 syllables each (anuṣṭubh).
lines_deva: बहु.भावो ऽनुरागो वा सारो वा कार्य.साधकः

words.gloss: the possession of good qualities by the remaining constituent elements

hindi: किन्तु दोनों का व्यसन समान होने पर गुणों की हानि के अनुसार विशेषता होती है, यदि शेष प्रकृतियों की सद्गुणता अविधेय न हो।
english: But when the calamity of two is equal, the distinction is according to the loss of qualities, provided that the possession of good qualities by the remaining constituent elements would not be unamenable.
notes: guṇataḥ kṣayāt is read together: 'from loss in respect of qualities'. sādguṇya here is 'possession of good qualities' (sad-guṇa), not ṣāḍguṇya the sixfold policy. The sense of the second half-line (na avidheyakam) is obscure; rendered literally.
lines_deva: द्वयोस् तु व्यसने तुल्ये विशेषो गुणतः क्षयात्
lines_iast: dvayos tu vyasane tulye viśeṣo guṇataḥ kṣayāt

words.gloss: the destruction of the remaining constituent elements

hindi: किन्तु जहाँ एक के व्यसन से शेष प्रकृतियों का नाश हो जाए, वहाँ वह व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर होता है, चाहे वह प्रधान प्रकृति का हो या अन्य का।
english: But where the destruction of the remaining constituent elements would result from the calamity of one, that calamity would be the graver, whether it be of the principal one or of another.
lines_deva: व्यसनं तद् गरीयः स्यात् प्रधानस्य-इतरस्य वा
lines_iast: vyasanaṃ tad garīyaḥ syāt pradhānasya-itarasya vā
